name: Invitation Intro Question Loops
use_when: The video is a long-form documentary, essay, travel film, or high-trust creator piece where world, tone, and curiosity are part of the value.
The opening can raise specific visual questions and answer at least one early enough to earn viewer trust.
The explicit promise would feel weaker if delivered before the viewer feels the world and conflict.
avoid_when: The deliverable is a short-form feed video, direct-response ad, or simple tutorial where the viewer needs the payoff immediately.
The opening is merely confusing and does not create clear questions.
The edit cannot close or reframe the questions it opens.
The creator has not earned enough trust for a slow invitation.

timeline_pattern.pattern: curious_first_frame -> multiple_question_loops -> early_loop_closure -> expanded_questions -> worldbuilding -> conflict_or_proof -> call_to_adventure -> explicit_promise
timeline_pattern.first_frame_rule: The first frame must give the viewer something useful: a question, tension, location clue, strange action, or sensory contradiction.
timeline_pattern.trust_rule: Close at least one loop early so the audience believes later loops will also be answered.
timeline_pattern.promise_rule: Delay the full promise only while the edit is actively building curiosity, world, conflict, or trust.
timeline_pattern.scope_rule: This is a long-form invitation pattern, not a replacement for feed-first hook clarity.

motion.rule: Use movement, framing, and visual distortion to raise questions only when they connect to the world or conflict.
motion.avoid: Random glitch, shake, or speed effects that create confusion without a story question.

sound.rule: Use distorted sound, tonal swells, ambience, or selective silence to make the opening feel like an invitation into a world.
sound.timing: Answer one loop before the sound bed becomes exhausting or opaque.

captions.rule: Captions may clarify location or key words, but should not explain away the mystery before the loop has value.
captions.avoid: Covering the opening image, map, proof shot, or facial/body-language clue.

color.rule: Use color or treatment to support the world's tone while preserving important clues and evidence.

implementation.ffmpeg: Create a first-minute contact sheet and mark each shot as question, answer, world, conflict, proof, or promise. Check whether at least one answer appears before the sequence asks too much.
implementation.remotion: Represent open loops as objects with id, question, openedAt, closedAt, closureType, and trustValue. Render a debug overlay during review, then disable it for export.
implementation.blender: Use camera moves, environmental scale, or restrained distortion to create curiosity; avoid abstract motion with no loop to close.
implementation.capcut_equivalent: Build the intro from question shots and early answer shots instead of starting with a loud promise montage.
implementation.premiere_equivalent: Use markers named open_loop, early_closure, worldbuilding, conflict, proof, call_to_adventure, and promise_delivery.

common_mistakes: Opening several loops without closing one early.
Delaying the promise while adding filler instead of worldbuilding.
Using this pattern for short-form videos that need immediate premise clarity.
Hiding the subject so completely that the viewer cannot tell what kind of video they are watching.
qc: Does the first frame create a specific question or tension?
Is at least one early loop closed before more questions stack up?
Can the editor name every open loop in the intro?
Does the delayed promise feel earned by world, conflict, proof, or trust?
Would the same intro still work if watched without prior knowledge of the creator?
